H.N.Anand represented by his General Power of Attorney I.R.Hegde.

In the description of the property mentioned in Ex.P.3, it is clearly stated that here is 10 squares RCC house consisting of Mosaic O.S.No.5243/2018 C/w 6502/2018 flooring, doors, windows and having civil amenities was purchased by the plaintiff Dr.H.N.Anand.

18. Ex.P.4 is the encumbrance certificate produced to show that the defendant No.1 Christopher Santos has fraudulently sold the suit property in favour of M.Sathish and M.Sandeep on 21-2-2018.

The disputed document is produced by the plaintiff and marked as Ex.P.5, wherein, the first defendant Christopher Santos claims himself as Power of Attorney and executed sale deed in favour of first and second defendant.

The Power of Attorney alleged to have been executed by Dr.Anand in his favour is an unregistered Power of Attorney and in view of Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court,
in Suraj Lamp & Industries (P) Ltd. v. State of Haryana (Suraj Lamp reported in (2009) 7 SCC 363 passed on on 15 May, 2009 I), a two- Judge Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court declared "power of attorney" sales to be an invalid mode of property transfer.

sentences.text: The Court conclusively stated that the parties could not effectuate a valid sale by executing a power of attorney, nor by O.S.No.5243/2018 C/w 6502/2018 entering into a sale agreement (SA) which was followed by a power of attorney (GPA) and will - a transaction termed as SA/GPA/will transfer.
The Power of Attorney holder cannot convey better title.

Firstly,
based on unregistered GPA, this Ex.P.5 is executed.

Secondly the execution of GPA has specifically disputed by the plaintiff Dr.H.N.Anand.

each was paid by the defendant Nos.2 and 3 under the D.D and cheque numbers mentioned in page No.4.

However, the contesting defendants have not produced any materials to show that any single amount is paid directly to Dr.H.N.Anand.
Therefore, the sale deed is not supported by consideration and does not convey the better title in favour of the defendant Nos.2 and 3 i.e., M.Sathish and M.Sandeep.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The Society has executed lease cum sale agreement on 30-1-1983 and the society has delivered the possession to L.V.Subramanyam.
He constructed 100 square building over the site No.51 based on lease cum sale agreement.
The Bengaluru Development Authority executed Sale Deed on 28-05-1987 in respect of the entire extent of 30 acres in favour of the Bank Officers Co-operative Housing Society and Society has formally issued possession certificate to the O.S.No.5243/2018 C/w 6502/2018 vendor of the plaintiff L.V.Subramanyam on 20-02-1988 in respect of the suit property.
It is the further case of the plaintiff that his vendor L.V.Subramanyam was in need of money for his legal and family necessity and also to acquire another property, intended to sell the suit property.
The plaintiff intended to purchase the suit schedule property.
Therefore, a sale deed was executed by L.V.Subramanyam in respect of the suit property in favour of the plaintiff on 20-06-2001.
The plaintiff is Doctor by profession, he is settled in United Kingdom, he was not able to personally manage the property.
The complaint was registered in C.R.No.130/2018 against the first defendant and others for the offenses punishable under Section 420, 465, 417, 471, 468 R/w Section 34 of Old Indian Penal Code.
In the written statement of first defendant, he categorically denied the plaint averments in toto.
He admitted the fact that the plaintiff was the owner of the suit property.
However, he claimed that the plaintiff executed GPA in his favour and based on the Power granted by the plaintiff, he sold the suit property in favour of the defendant Nos.2 and 3 and delivered the possession to the defendant Nos.2 and 3.
The first defendant claimed that he has not committed any fraud, forgery and legally executed the sale deed in favour of defendant Nos.2 and 3.
The first defendant sought to dismiss the suit.
The first defendant on the authority given by the plaintiff executed the sale deed in their favour by receiving the valuable consideration.
The first defendant delivered the possession of the suit schedule property in favour of them and they are in actual possession and enjoyment of the same.
Since the plaintiff and the Power of Attorney Holder of the plaintiff interfered with their possession, they have filed O.S.No.65608/2018 which was pending before CCH-18.
They contended that the katha was changed in their name and they are paying property tax to the BBMP.
Therefore, the plaintiff or his power of attorney has no right,
O.S.No.5243/2018 C/w 6502/2018 title or interest over the suit property.
The plaintiffs claimed that BDA has allotted 30 acres of land in Sy.No.12 and 14 of Tavarekere village to the Bank Officer's Co- operative Housing Society Limited as per lease cum sale agreement on 13-01-1983.
Subsequently, possession certificate was issued in favour of L.V.Subramanyam on 20-2-1988.
L.V.Subramanyam, the owner of suit schedule property has conveyed the suit schedule property in favour of the defendant No.2 through registered sale deed, dated 20-6-2001.
The first defendant has conveyed the suit schedule property through defendant No.3 in favour of the plaintiff for valuable consideration under the Sale Deed, dated 27-2-2018.
Thus, the plaintiffs became lawful owners and possessors of suit property.
The plaintiffs claimed that based on the sale deed, katha was transferred in their name and they are paying property tax to the BBMP.
They are in physical and lawful possession of the suit property.
The plaintiffs claimed that the defendant Nos.1, 3 on the instigation of defendant No.2 tried to take forcible possession of suit property from the plaintiffs on 30-08-2018 and 1-9-2018.
They took the law in their hands and threatening the plaintiffs to vacate the suit property.
Therefore, they filed this suit for permanent injunction sought to decree the suit.
The third defendant cannot convey better title in favour of the plaintiffs based on fraudulent document.
Both the defendant Nos.1 and 2 claimed that they are in physical possession and enjoyment of the suit property and sought to dismiss the suit.
opennyai_summary.issue:
5. Based on the pleadings, my Predecessor in office has framed the following issues:-
1.
Whether the plaintiff proves that he is the absolute owner of suit property?
2. Whether plaintiff proves that his signature is forged by defendant No.1 on the GPA dated 08-10-2001?
3. Whether the plaintiff proves that he has never executed GPA in favour of defendant No.1 on 8-10-2001?
4. Whether plaintiff proves that the registered sale deed dated 27-02-2018 executed by defendant No.1 in favour of defendant Nos.2 and 3 in respect of suit property is null and void not binding on him?
5. Whether plaintiff proves that the registered Rectification Deed dated 21-03-2018 executed by defendant No.4 in favour of defendant Nos.2 and 3 in respect of suit property is null and void not binding on him?
6. Whether plaintiff is entitled for suit reliefs?
7. What Order or decree?
Whether the plaintiffs prove that they are in O.S.No.5243/2018 C/w 6502/2018 possession and enjoyment of the suit schedule property?
2. Whether the plaintiffs prove that the defendants are interfering with suit schedule property?
3. Whether the plaintiffs are entitled for the reliefs as prayed?
opennyai_summary.arguments:
The dispute is in respect of the execution of the sale deed by the first defendant in O.S.No.5243/2018 in favour of the defendant Nos.2 and 3 of the said case and subsequently, the execution of Rectification Deed by the Secretary of the society in favour of the defendant Nos.2 and 3 in O.S.No.5243/2018.
15.
The plaintiff H.N.Anand alleged that his signature was forged in the alleged GPA with active connivance of the first defendant N.Vishwanath in collusion with defendant Nos.2 and 3.
Therefore, the plaintiff sought Sale Deed dated 27-2-2018 and the Rectification Deed dated 21-3-2018 is null and void and not binding on his share.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The Power of Attorney alleged to have been executed by Dr.Anand in his favour is an unregistered Power of Attorney and in view of Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court,
in Suraj Lamp & Industries (P) Ltd. v. State of Haryana (Suraj Lamp reported in (2009) 7 SCC 363 passed on on 15 May, 2009 I), a two- Judge Bench of the Hon'ble Supreme Court declared "power of attorney" sales to be an invalid mode of property transfer.
The Court conclusively stated that the parties could not effectuate a valid sale by executing a power of attorney, nor by O.S.No.5243/2018 C/w 6502/2018 entering into a sale agreement (SA) which was followed by a power of attorney (GPA) and will - a transaction termed as SA/GPA/will transfer.
The Power of Attorney holder cannot convey better title.
Secondly the execution of GPA has specifically disputed by the plaintiff Dr.H.N.Anand.
19.
There is no necessity for the society to execute the Rectification Deed as per Ex.P.6.
